# SaveGame

14 tools. Back to the [index](README.md).

## `create_save_game`

Create a new SaveGame instance from a specified SaveGame class

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `save_game_class` | string | no | Optional SaveGame subclass; defaults to the plugin's concrete UMCPSaveGame (the abstract USaveGame base is rejected) |

**Returns:** `{ save_game_class: string, save_game_instance: string, save_game_path: string, success: bool }`

## `list_save_games`

List all save games for a given user index. The list is what the platform's save system calls slots: on desktop, the .sav files at the root of the save folder. A save system can also keep a slot as a FOLDER of .sav files, which is not a slot here: those folders are reported apart, in slot_folders, so an empty list is only proof of no save when slot_folders is empty too.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `user_index` | number | no | Optional user index, default 0. Passed to the platform's save system; the generic desktop one keeps every user's slots in one folder, so there it changes nothing. |

**Returns:** `{ user_index: int, save_directory: string, save_games: [{ slot_name, file_path?, file_size? }], count: int, slot_folders: [{ folder, sav_files }] (subfolders of save_directory holding .sav files, searched recursively) }`

## `load_game`

Load a SaveGame instance from a named slot

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `slot_name` | string | yes | Save slot name to load from |
| `user_index` | number | no | Optional user index, default 0 |
| `save_game_class` | string | no | Optional SaveGame subclass the slot is expected to hold. A slot file records its own class and is rebuilt as that; when the loaded object is not this class (or a child of it) the load is reported as failed. An unknown class name is an error. |

**Returns:** `{ slot_name: string, user_index: int, success: bool, save_game_instance: string, save_game_class: string, save_game_path: string, expected_class?: string, error: string }`

## `restore_actor_state`

Restore the transform + properties a previous serialize_actor_state wrote, addressed by the SAME key it was saved under. Idempotent: restoring twice in a row re-applies the same values both times. It restores only what was captured -- if serialize_actor_state was called without property_names, this puts back the transform and nothing else.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `actor_name_or_stable_key` | string | yes | Required. The stable_key used at serialize time (or the actor_name, when no explicit stable_key was passed to serialize_actor_state). The actor to restore ONTO is then resolved from the actor_name stored inside the saved payload, looked up in the current world. |

**Returns:** `{ restored: bool, properties_restored: [string], transform_restored: bool }`

## `serialize_actor_state`

Save an actor's transform plus an EXPLICIT set of properties into a SaveGame slot, keyed by an identity YOU choose (stable_key, defaulting to actor_name). Nothing is captured implicitly: name the properties you want in property_names or you get the transform and only the transform. Idempotent -- re-serializing the same key overwrites that slot, it never duplicates. Pair with restore_actor_state, which takes the same key.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `actor_name` | string | yes | Required. Object name or editor label of the actor to serialize (resolved via mcp_common::FindActorByName). |
| `stable_key` | string | no | Optional. Identity used as the persistence key; defaults to actor_name. The caller owns this key on purpose: AActor::GetActorGuid() is editor-only and not documented as stable across level reloads, so no GUID key is auto-generated for you. |
| `property_names` | array | no | Optional array of UPROPERTY names to capture in addition to the transform. If omitted, ONLY the transform is saved -- it never silently saves "everything" via CPF_SaveGame, which no native property here sets and which, on a Blueprint variable, depends on whether that Blueprint ticked the SaveGame checkbox (get_blueprint_variable_detailed_info reports it): a filter this command cannot assume for you. |

**Returns:** `{ slot_id: string, saved: bool, property_count: int }`
